question.text: How many executive orders will the US president sign during December 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the total number of numbered Executive Orders that are officially published in the [Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/presidential-documents/executive-orders/donald-trump/2026) and signed by the US president during December 2026.
question.fine_print:
Presidential Memoranda, Presidential Proclamations, Presidential Determinations, Administrative Orders, National Security Presidential Memoranda, and any other presidential documents that are not formally designated as "Executive Orders" do not count toward resolution.

Orders that are later revoked still count toward the total.

Orders that are blocked by courts still count toward the total.

research:
I've finished the research. The main finding is that, as far as the Federal Register shows, Trump has signed no numbered executive orders since October 22, 2026, almost four weeks. That's well below the 2026 average of about 7 a month. Every past December I checked had 3 to 11.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-18: A Federal Register API query (EOs signed since 2026-06-01) shows the latest is **EO 14438, "Decreasing Housing Costs for the American People," signed 2026-10-22 and published 2026-10-28**. None are listed with a November 2026 signing date. [FR API](https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents.csv?conditions[presidential_document_type]=executive_order&conditions[signing_date][gte]=2026-06-01&per_page=200&fields[]=executive_order_number&fields[]=signing_date&fields[]=publication_date&fields[]=title&order=newest)
- 2026-11-18: The White House EO page also shows 14438 (Oct 22) as the newest. [whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/executive-orders/)
- October 2026 count: 4 (Oct 5, 16, 19, 22). Your background list stops at September.
- Today's Federal Register public inspection file has no presidential documents in it. [FR public inspection](https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/public-inspection-documents/current.json)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing about December can be settled yet. The relevant signal is a lull: no EOs from about Oct 23 to Nov 18.
- 2026-11-05: Trump signed an order on the Oval Office and Cabinet Room. The White House caption calls it an "Executive Order," but CTV reports it was a **proclamation**, which would not count. [CTV](https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/article/trump-signs-proclamation-he-says-will-prevent-future-changes-to-the-oval-office-and-cabinet-room/), [WH gallery](https://www.whitehouse.gov/gallery/president-donald-j-trump-signs-an-executive-order-designating-the-oval-office-and-cabinet-room-as-national-landmarks/)

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-11-16: The Supreme Court agreed to hear three immigration cases involving Trump EOs during its 2026-27 term. [CBC](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/us-scotus-major-immigration-cases-9.7423295)
- Early November 2026: Democrats won control of Congress in the midterms (CTV coverage of the Nov 5 order). A Democratic Congress could lead to more governing by executive action, or to a quiet lame-duck period. [CTV](https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/article/trump-signs-proclamation-he-says-will-prevent-future-changes-to-the-oval-office-and-cabinet-room/)
- 2026-11-16: The US and 9 other countries signed the Pax Silica AI supply-chain declaration. This is an AI policy topic that could later lead to an EO. [Telegraph India](https://www.telegraphindia.com/world/india-united-states-join-eight-nations-to-strengthen-artificial-intelligence-supply-chains-amid-china-competition/cid/2189660)
- I found no reporting that explains the lull or says a batch of orders is being prepared.

## 4. Base rates (December counts, from Federal Register signing dates)
- December 2017: 4. December 2018: 5. December 2019: 3. December 2020: 11 (lame duck). December 2025: 8. [FR API](https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents.csv?conditions[presidential_document_type]=executive_order&conditions[president]=donald-trump&conditions[signing_date][gte]=2017-12-01&conditions[signing_date][lte]=2020-12-31&per_page=500&fields[]=executive_order_number&fields[]=signing_date&order=newest)
- December 2025 included two routine year-end orders: EO 14368, "Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay" (Dec 18), and EO 14371, closing federal agencies on Dec 24 and 26 (Dec 18). [FR API](https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents.csv?conditions[presidential_document_type]=executive_order&conditions[signing_date][gte]=2025-11-01&conditions[signing_date][lte]=2026-01-31&per_page=200&fields[]=executive_order_number&fields[]=signing_date&fields[]=title&order=newest)
  - The annual pay-adjustment EO appeared in late December in 2017, 2018 and 2025, which makes at least 1 December EO likely.
  - Holiday-closing EOs are discretionary.
- Monthly pattern in 2026: 10, 8, 10, 4, 5, 6, 2, 7, 11, 4 (Jan to Oct), averaging about 6.7. November so far is 0. The trend since spring is lower and more volatile, with lows of 2 (July) and 0 so far in November.
- Seasonality: December has been at or above the median month in 2020 and 2025, and lower (3 to 5) in 2017 to 2019. This year is running well below 2025's pace: November 2025 had 7 EOs, November 2026 has 0 so far.
- The question's range tops out at 10.5. December 2020 (11) would have gone over it.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Manifold, "How many EOs in November 2026": 0-2 at 14%, 3-4 at 18%, 5-6 at 18%, 7-8 at 18%, 9-10 at 18%, 11+ at 14%. This is thinly traded and close to the default spread. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Terminator2/how-many-executive-orders-will-trum-Qut9UpS9O2)
- Kalshi weekly EO markets for Nov 1-7 and Nov 8-14, 2026: "Above 0" at 1%. This is consistent with zero EOs in those weeks; they look settled at No.
- Kalshi, second-term total: the most likely bucket is 400-449 (25%), then 350-399 (20%). The current count is about 213 (14438 minus 14147 plus 1, roughly 292 across both years).
  - Correction: the second-term total so far is about 292 EOs (14148 to 14438 plus 14147). Getting to 400 by January 2029 needs about 4.5 a month.
- Polymarket, "Trump issues AI Restrictions EO by Dec 31": 13%. By Nov 30: 0.7%.
- I found no Kalshi or Polymarket market on December 2026 EO counts specifically.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Mid to late December: the annual federal pay-rate adjustment EO is expected, as in 2017, 2018 and 2025. A possible Christmas Eve or Dec 26 closure EO could also come.
- The lame-duck Congress and government funding deadlines could trigger EOs. A new Democratic Congress takes office Jan 3, 2027, after resolution.
- Possible AI EO (Polymarket gives 13% by Dec 31), plus tariff or sanctions follow-ups.
- Federal Register publication lag is about 3 to 6 days. EOs signed in late December may not be published until early January, which matters for when the question can resolve.
- Weather is not relevant.

(b) **Latest known value:** The newest EO in the Federal Register is EO 14438, signed 2026-10-22. As of 2026-11-18 there are no EOs with a November signing date. October had 4.

(c) **If nothing changed:** The lull would continue and December would have 0. However, the annual pay-adjustment EO has appeared in late December every year checked (2017, 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2025). So "nothing changed" realistically means about 1.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** The trend since spring is lower and volatile: 4, 5, 6, 2, 7, 11, 4, then 0 so far in November. That points to about 2 to 4 in December, including the routine pay order and possibly a holiday-closure order.

(e) **Historical variation:** Past December counts were 4, 5, 3, 11 and 8. The 2026 monthly counts ranged from 2 to 11, and the current month-to-date is 0. The spread is wide.

(f) **Experts and markets:** There is no market on December counts.
- The Kalshi second-term total market (mode 400 to 449, against about 292 so far) implies roughly 4 to 5 per month on average.
- The Manifold November market is near its default spread and not informative.
- Kalshi weekly markets confirm zero EOs in early November.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** The lull persists through the holidays, perhaps because of the president's health, a strategic pause after the midterms, or a shift to proclamations and memoranda. The pay adjustment could come by another vehicle or slip to January, giving 0.
- **High:** Facing a Democratic Congress arriving January 3, the administration rushes a batch of executive actions in the lame-duck period, on AI, tariffs, immigration and the funding fight. Together with the pay and closure orders, that could give 10 to 15, as in December 2020 (11).
